professionalSummary.title: Professional Summary
professionalSummary.content:
Fullstack developer student at Teknikhögskolan (2-year YH program) with a primary focus on Java backend development and React frontend. Experienced in building structured, maintainable applications with emphasis on clean architecture, RESTful APIs, and database design.

Strong foundation in databases, security principles, DevOps and DevSecOps practices, including CI/CD workflows and version control using Git with structured branching strategies. Accustomed to working in agile environments with iterative development, code reviews, and collaborative teamwork.

Driven by problem-solving, continuous learning, and writing scalable, secure, and production-oriented code.

project1.title: Budget Tracker
project1.description: A Java Spring Boot application for tracking personal finances by managing income and expenses with structured budget categories.

project2.title: Plantswap
project2.description: A Spring Boot marketplace application enabling users to buy, sell, and trade plants with other enthusiasts in a community-driven platform.

project3.title: Homi
project3.description: A collaborative full-stack Airbnb clone built with a team of 3 developers. Features property listings, user authentication, and booking system with separate backend and frontend repositories.

project4.title: HealthcareSDLC
project4.description: A collaborative healthcare booking application developed by a team of 4, emphasizing SDLC methodology, DevOps, and DevSecOps practices with automated CI/CD pipelines and code quality monitoring.

project5.title: Finance Tracker
project5.description: A comprehensive personal finance tracking application developed as a solo project, featuring full CI/CD implementation, automated testing, and code quality checks. Manages expenses, income, budgets, and financial goals.

project6.title: Personality Miner
project6.description: Thesis project investigating which method – RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), fine-tuning, or structured prompting – is most effective for guiding a local Large Language Model (LLM) to stay within defined ethical boundaries during psychological self-reflection.
